title: Electron Spin Notation (↑ ↓) & Shell Mapping Matrices
notes: **Arrowhead vector notation:** electrons are drawn as arrowheads — an upward arrow (↑) represents spin +½ (clockwise) and a downward arrow (↓) represents spin −½ (anticlockwise); each box (orbital) can hold at most two arrows of opposite direction.

**Net zero paired magnetic field cancellation:** when an orbital contains two electrons with opposite spins, their magnetic moments are equal and opposite, so the net magnetic field of the pair is zero — the atom as a whole becomes diamagnetic for that pair.

**K shell complete mapping matrix:** the K shell (n = 1) contains only the single 1s orbital; it is filled as 1s¹ (one ↑) for hydrogen and 1s² (↑↓) for helium, where the pair is fully spin-compensated.

**L shell complete mapping matrix:** the L shell (n = 2) contains the 2s orbital plus three 2p orbitals (2pₓ, 2pᵧ, 2p_z). Filling follows Hund's rule — electrons first occupy each orbital singly with parallel spins before pairing: e.g. oxygen (1s² 2s² 2p⁴) shows one paired 2p box (↑↓) and two half-filled boxes (↑, ↑).

**Arrow direction convention:** in electron configuration notation the order of filling is drawn left-to-right across the orbitals of the subshell, and the last electron added determines the arrow direction for half-filled orbitals.
